target.title: refactor: consolidate generic number clamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first number-coercion consolidation pass in #99671 migrated finite-number and integer option callers, but generic inclusive clamp mechanics still had a legacy implementation in `src/utils.ts` plus exact local copies in agents and the Control UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

This makes `@openclaw/normalization-core/number-coercion` the canonical owner for policy-free numeric clamping and removes exact local copies. The existing `clamp`, `clampInt`, and `clampNumber` function declarations remain in `src/utils.ts` as a published compatibility facade and delegate to normalization-core; keeping those declarations also preserves the plugin SDK callable-surface contract. Finite-number validation in the touched Control UI path now uses the existing canonical helper. Units, defaults, fallback/error policy, domain bounds, retry policy, and semantic sentinels remain local.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. The same inclusive bounds and integer-flooring contracts now share one implementation while current plugin SDK exports remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the prior exact-head CI failure from `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2`: `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` detected six missing callable facade declarations.
- Fixed tooling contract: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`
  - Result: 1 shard passed; 8 tests passed.
- Focused callers: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.test.ts src/utils.test.ts src/logging/log-tail.test.ts src/agents/memory-search.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/bash-command.stop.test.ts src/agents/code-mode.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.adds-claude-style-aliases-schemas-without-dropping-g.test.ts ui/src/ui/chat/grouped-render.test.ts`
  - Result: 7 Vitest shards passed; 212 tests passed.
- Testbox-through-Crabbox: `tbx_01kwnk58e0c08hhkyhypb7aw5h`, Actions run `28693714269`, exit 0.
  - `pnpm check:changed` passed core production/test typechecks, lint with zero warnings/errors, guards, duplicate coverage, and import-cycle checks.
  - Full `pnpm build` passed, including plugin SDK export validation and Control UI build.
- Fresh exact-branch autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; correctness confidence 0.98.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Production LOC: 32 additions, 31 deletions; net +1. The compatibility facade accounts for the one-line growth while duplicate local clamp bodies are removed.

target.title: fix(qa): stabilize primary smoke runtime evidence
target.body:
Related: #99705
Related: #99737
Related: #99368

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two recent QA Smoke CI regressions while preserving the stronger primary runtime coverage:

1. Smoke-linked Docker scenarios each rebuilt the complete OpenClaw package, growing the lane from roughly 5–6 minutes to 11–13 minutes and sometimes exhausting the 8 GB Node heap.
2. #99737 converted `qa-otel-smoke` to executable script evidence, but the profile runner expands `${outputDir}` to an absolute path while the child `qa suite` CLI requires a repo-relative output path. That made current-main smoke runs fail after all gateway scenarios and both Docker scenarios had passed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Prepare one validated candidate tarball before the profile and expose it through the existing `OPENCLAW_CURRENT_PACKAGE_TGZ` Docker E2E contract.
- Keep all six release-category scenarios on Docker; taxonomy category IDs remain the single source of truth for profile selection.
- Give the single package build a 12 GB Node heap to clear the observed 8 GB `tsdown` ceiling.
- Translate the OTEL producer's outer artifact path into the repo-relative form required by its child QA command, while rejecting paths outside the repository.

This does not move primary evidence back to focused Vitest tests and does not add a profile-specific scenario allowlist.

## User Impact

Contributors retain packaged-runtime Docker coverage without duplicate package builds. The OTEL runtime producer can also run correctly through the profile's shared script adapter instead of deterministically failing after the rest of the smoke profile succeeds.

## Evidence

- Before Docker regression: sampled June 26 QA Smoke jobs completed in approximately 4m40s–6m27s.
- After #99705/#99736: sampled July 4 jobs took approximately 10m22s–13m33s; failed artifacts showed independent `tsdown` package builds approaching the 8 GB heap ceiling.
- Full Testbox-through-Crabbox profile with shared package: package 1m32s, profile 2m57s, full command 5m07s; both Docker scenarios passed.
  - Testbox: `tbx_01kwnj0ja36rjm5r9gyah51xbj`
  - Actions run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28693254338
- First rebased 4-vCPU PR run: both Docker scenarios and all 25 isolated gateway scenarios passed; `qa-otel-smoke` then failed solely because the absolute profile artifact path violated the child CLI contract.
  - Actions run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28693422540
- Exact failing OTEL command shape with an absolute outer output path now passes locally: 17 spans, 26 metrics, 17 OTLP logs, and 17 stdout logs.
- Focused Vitest proof: 131/131 passed across workflow guards, scenario catalog, package helper, Docker lane adapter, and OTEL producer tests.
- `git diff --check` and focused `oxfmt --check` — passed.
- Final structured Codex autoreview — no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct at 0.96 confidence.
